correctness.rationale: Every simple hexagon corresponds bijectively to a Fano noncollinear triple; a generic six-walk enumeration independently agrees on all 28 masks. The Heawood cycle-space dimension is 8 and a spanning tree provides a verified exact coordinate bijection. All 256 reduced character sums are explicitly evaluated twice by independent algorithms; the histogram leads to full 2^21 spectrum with factor 2^13. The exact projection kernel has integer absolute mass 1936 over 256 points, and averaging any projection over group translations proves its 121/16 endpoint norm globally optimal. Fully covered finite enumeration is used only for finite claims; no infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The canonical Heawood graph is the unique cubic girth-six cage and the Fano incidence graph, so its shortest-cycle edge code is a natural, symmetry-rich object. Exact rank (1212416), invisible modes (884736) and optimum recovery projection norm (121/16) describe intrinsic Fourier information loss and best possible endpoint stability. These values are not immediate from the twenty-eight-cycle count or ordinary adjacency spectra. A finite complete classification and a small standalone 256-state certificate offer reusable information for parity-based measurements on graph cycle codes; significance is restricted to this canonical graph.
